definition: DeCS – Health Sciences Descriptors is a structured and trilingual thesaurus created by BIREME – Latin American and Caribbean Center on Health Sciences Information – in 1986 for indexing scientific journal articles, books, proceedings of congresses, technical reports and other types of materials, as well as for searching and recovering scientific information in LILACS, MEDLINE and other databases.
details: In the VHL, Virtual Health Library, DeCS is the tool that permits the navigation between records and sources of information through controlled concepts and organized in Portuguese, Spanish and English. It was developed from MeSH – Medical Subject Headings from the NLM – U.S. National Library of Medicine – in order to permit the use of common terminology for searching in three languages, providing a consistent and unique environment for information retrieval regardless of the language. In addition to the original MeSH terms, four specific areas were developed: Public Health (1986), Homeopathy (1991), Health Surveillance (2005), and Science and Health (2005). The concepts that compose the DeCS vocabulary are organized in a hierarchical structure permitting searches in broader or more specific terms or all the terms that belong to a single hierarchy. Its main purpose is to serve as a unique language for indexing and recovery of information among the components of the Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Information System, coordinated by BIREME and that encompasses 37 countries in Latin America and the Caribbean, permitting a uniform dialog between nearly 600 libraries. explainer.lead: Health Sciences Descriptors, or DeCS, is a shared vocabulary for describing and finding health-science information in Portuguese, Spanish, and English. It lets the same concept connect records across languages and databases, making searches more consistent.

tiers.eli5: Imagine several libraries using different words and languages for the same health topic. DeCS gives everyone a shared label for that topic, like giving matching stickers to books about the same thing. It also groups related stickers from big topics to smaller ones, so you can look broadly or narrow your search.
tiers.practitioner: Indexers assign DeCS descriptors to journal articles, books, conference proceedings, technical reports, and other materials; searchers then use those controlled concepts in the Virtual Health Library, LILACS, MEDLINE, and other databases. Searches can move through the hierarchy to broader or narrower terms and work across Portuguese, Spanish, and English. A key pitfall is treating DeCS as an ordinary keyword list rather than a controlled, hierarchical vocabulary derived from MeSH.
tiers.paperLevel: DeCS is a structured trilingual thesaurus: each controlled concept has terminology in Portuguese, Spanish, and English and occupies a position in a hierarchy supporting broader, narrower, or whole-branch retrieval. BIREME created it in 1986 from the U.S. National Library of Medicine's MeSH, adding Public Health in 1986, Homeopathy in 1991, and Health Surveillance and Science and Health in 2005. Its scope is coordinated indexing and retrieval within the Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Information System.

explainer.example: A technical report is indexed with a descriptor from DeCS's Homeopathy area. A searcher can find that record using the corresponding Portuguese, Spanish, or English terminology, then broaden or narrow the search by moving through the descriptor's hierarchy.

explainer.intuition: DeCS acts like a shared map of health topics: one concept can be reached through Portuguese, Spanish, or English, and its place in the map shows related broader and narrower topics.
howItWorks: Start with MeSH terminology and additional health-science areas.
Represent concepts in Portuguese, Spanish, and English.
Assign descriptors when indexing documents and records.
Retrieve records by concept, language, or hierarchy level.
explainer.whyItMatters: A common controlled vocabulary reduces language and terminology differences between indexers and searchers. It supports consistent information exchange across BIREME's regional system and nearly 600 libraries.
misconceptions: DeCS is derived from MeSH, not created independently of it.
It is a hierarchical controlled vocabulary, not just a translation list.
It covers materials beyond journal articles, including books and technical reports.
